subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw stop force-refreshing inside Codex app-server account/chatgptAuthTokens/refresh callbacks and instead answer within Codex's 10-second contract from cached-valid credentials or a typed fail-fast auth error?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses OpenClaw auth freshness policy and the upstream Codex app-server timeout contract, and repository policy treats fallback/auth behavior as a product decision rather than an implementation convenience.

options.title: Answer within callback contract
options.body: Reuse still-valid canonical OAuth credentials for the callback and return parseable reauth errors when refresh is truly required but cannot complete in time.

options.title: Coordinate upstream timeout change
options.body: Keep OpenClaw force-refresh semantics and rely on an upstream Codex configurable or longer callback timeout to absorb slow refreshes.

options.title: Fold into broader auth incident work
options.body: Pause this narrow item and let broader profile quarantine/status work own the user-visible recovery path, accepting that the exact callback timeout remains until then.

recommendation.title: Answer within callback contract
recommendation.body: Reuse still-valid canonical OAuth credentials for the callback and return parseable reauth errors when refresh is truly required but cannot complete in time.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision most directly concerns the canonical OAuth routing and Codex auth bridge surfaces tied to recent vincentkoc-authored history.
